claims.text: Raymond James's recruiting page (page content as of April 21, 2026) lists the AdvisorChoice® affiliation options as Traditional Employee, Advisor Select, Independent Contractor, Bank & Credit Union, and Corporate RIA, describing Traditional Employee as offering book ownership, Advisor Select as leading one's own branch, Independent Contractor as operating as an independent financial advisor, Bank & Credit Union as leveraging national strength, and Corporate RIA as exercising true autonomy.

The same recruiting page (content as of April 21, 2026) states the affiliation spectrum also includes an RIA & Custody Services option, described as 'Take strategic, financial and administrative control of your practice with a full-service partner at the ready.'

A graphic in the investor-day deck (published June 5, 2025) lists the AdvisorChoice spectrum as Employee Advisor (RJA), Advisor Select, Independent Advisor (ICD), Banks and Credit Unions, IAR (Corporate RIA), and RIA & Custody Services.

The 2025 Form 10-K (fiscal year ended September 30, 2025) states that financial advisors primarily affiliate directly as either employees or independent contractors, or as employees of third-party RIAs and broker-dealers served through the RIA and Custody Services (RCS) division.

For the Traditional Employee option, the recruiting page (content as of April 21, 2026) states a payout of up to 50% plus a full array of competitive employee benefits, with compliance support provided by the branch manager and the home office.
For the Advisor Select option, the same page (content as of April 21, 2026) states a 70-80% gross payout and a full array of competitive employee benefits.
For the Independent Contractor option, the same page (content as of April 21, 2026) states an 81% to 90% payout, with benefits created through third-party partnerships.

For the Bank & Credit Union option, the recruiting page (content as of April 21, 2026) states advisors receive a competitive compensation package from the financial institution in partnership with Raymond James.
For the Corporate RIA option, the recruiting page (content as of April 21, 2026) states an 81% to 90% payout, with benefits created through third-party partnerships.

For the RIA & Custody Services option, the recruiting page (content as of April 21, 2026) states advisors work with their RIA or broker/dealer to determine compensation and create their own benefits package.

The 2025 Form 10-K (fiscal year ended September 30, 2025) states that compensation for employee financial advisors primarily includes a payout on the revenues they generate, and that such advisors also participate in the firm's employee benefit plans.

On the earnings call for the quarter ended March 31, 2026 (published April 22, 2026), management explained that independent payouts are higher because independent advisors cover their own overhead costs, such as real estate and health insurance, and that even the employee side has tiered payout systems where advisors move higher on the payout grid as production increases.

The 2025 Form 10-K (fiscal year ended September 30, 2025) states that Raymond James participates, with limited exceptions, in the Protocol for Broker Recruiting, a voluntary agreement among many firms that governs the client information financial advisors may take with them when they affiliate with a new firm and their ability to solicit clients of their prior firm.

The same 10-K describes an industry-wide trend in which financial advisors are departing traditional firms, including to form independent RIAs or to join existing third-party RIAs, some of which are backed by private equity investors.

The recruiting page (content as of April 21, 2026) describes AdvisorChoice® as a platform of dynamic options and the freedom to choose among them, letting advisors match their professional goals to the affiliation option that is right for them, with each option offering a unique combination of support, freedom, and flexibility.

On the earnings call for the quarter ended June 30, 2026 (published July 22, 2026), management said Raymond James has the largest addressable market in the industry because it has all the affiliation options an advisor could want and is agnostic—indifferent—about how advisors affiliate with the firm.

On the earnings call for the quarter ended June 30, 2025 (published July 23, 2025), management described the value proposition as 'best of both worlds'—an advisor- and client-focused culture coupled with leading technology and solutions—and said it continues to resonate with advisors across all affiliation options.

On the earnings call for the quarter ended December 31, 2025 (published January 28, 2026), management said the firm has the largest addressable market across its affiliation options, from employee to independent contractor to RIA custody, with critical mass and decades of experience in all of them.

On the earnings call for the quarter ended March 31, 2026 (published April 22, 2026), management stated its focus is to remain the absolute best destination for financial advisers and their clients across all of its affiliation options.
On the earnings call for the quarter ended June 30, 2026 (published July 22, 2026), management said growth remains focused on quality over quantity.

On the earnings call for the quarter ended June 30, 2026 (published July 22, 2026), management said recruiting is not something that can be turned on and off quarter to quarter, and requires consistency in retaining existing advisers, recruiting new advisers, and having the team focused on finding advisers who are good cultural fits with the firm across its affiliation options.

On the earnings call for the quarter ended December 31, 2025 (published January 28, 2026), management said recruited advisors come from competitor types including wires, regionals, and other independents, and described those firms as friendly competitors who are doing good jobs keeping their advisors.

On the earnings call for the quarter ended June 30, 2025 (published July 23, 2025), management identified private equity-backed roll-ups as a relatively novel competitive dynamic in advisor recruiting, saying they have been extremely aggressive in trading and paying at higher and higher multiples over the last three years in particular.

The 2025 Form 10-K (fiscal year ended September 30, 2025) names its direct competitors as other national full service broker-dealers, investment banking firms, commercial banks, investment advisors, investment managers, and, to a lesser extent, discount brokers and dealers, and notes competition from more recent entrants including fintechs.

On the earnings call for the quarter ended September 30, 2024 (published October 23, 2024), management said a couple of OSJ relationships in the independent contractor division had decided to leave the platform, and roughly $3 billion of AUA left the firm in the fiscal fourth quarter.
On the same call, the firm anticipated approximately $5 billion of assets associated with those departing OSJ firms would complete their transfers off the platform in early fiscal 2025.

On the earnings call for the quarter ended September 30, 2025 (published October 22, 2025), management said the firm would lose a platform through bank M&A the next quarter, approximately $2.7 billion of assets.

On the earnings call for the quarter ended December 31, 2024 (published January 29, 2025), management said the large departure previously discussed had essentially almost totally gone from the platform, and that it does not see anything big on the leaving side, though there is always some attrition.

The 2025 Form 10-K (fiscal year ended September 30, 2025) warns that financial advisors may leave the firm, including for independent RIAs or third-party RIAs, and that retiring financial advisors without a successor affiliated with the firm may sell their practices to unaffiliated third parties, which could negatively affect AUA.
